stories.headline: Bajaj family enters health care with Nivara, bets on care beyond hospitals
stories.title: Bajaj family enters health care with Nivara, bets on care beyond hospitals
stories.summary: The Bajaj family is making a new bet on India's health care market, but it does not want to build just another hospital chain. With Nivara, its health care venture, the group is attempting to build an integrated health care platform that puts outpatient care, diagnostics, home health care and day surgery at the centre of its business, with hospitals forming one part of a larger ecosystem.At the formal launch of Bajaj Integrated Health Systems (BIHS) on November 19, Nirav Bajaj, managing director of the venture, outlined an approach that he said was rooted in the group's values of putting patients first and taking a long-term view of business building. The group believes that nearly 70 percent of health care problems can be addressed outside hospitals, and wants to build its network around this premise.The first step will be a medical centre at Amanora in Pune, which is scheduled to open next week. The facility will bring together diagnostics, medical testing, doctor consultations and physiotherapy under one roof. Patients will be able to access their medical reports in one place, while the centre will also have a dedicated play area for children.The Pune launch is significant for a family that has deep roots in the city. Bajaj Auto and Bajaj Finance, two of the group's flagship businesses, are headquartered in Pune. The health care venture will initially use the city as a testing ground before taking its model to other markets. Nivara aims to establish a presence in six cities over 10 years.The next layer of the network will comprise home health care services and day-surgery centres. These centres will offer procedures and treatments such as dialysis, chemotherapy and endoscopy, among others, allowing patients to access services without having to visit a full-fledged hospital.Also Read: We are not focused solely on building large hospitals—we are building intelligent systems: Suneeta ReddyA 500-bed hospital is also planned in Pune, with construction expected to begin next year. It is likely to take three to four years to complete.The group had earlier announced an investment of ₹2,500 crore in its health care venture, which is being built as a continuum of care spanning neighbourhood medical centres, ambulatory facilities, home health care and multispecialty hospitals.One of the more interesting aspects of Nivara's proposed model is a subscription-based offering. Under this, customers would pay a monthly fee to cover their outpatient health care requirements. The company is also considering extending the offering to cover surgeries."We plan to add an option that allows subscription patients to be covered for everything, including surgeries," Bajaj said.The contours of this offering, including how it will be priced and whether the surgical component will involve an insurance arrangement, are yet to be spelt out. The distinction will be important in a market where outpatient expenses account for a significant part of household health care spending but are not adequately covered by traditional health insurance policies.The Bajaj group has an insurance business, but Bajaj clarified that it would operate independently of the health care venture. Nivara would deal with all insurance providers on an equal footing, with the relationship being conducted at arm's length.The opportunity is considerable. According to a March 2024 report by Bain & Company, India's overall health care market was valued at approximately $180 billion in FY23 and was projected to grow at around 12 percent annually to reach $320 billion by FY28. The report also estimated the health care innovation opportunity at $30 billion in FY23, with the potential to double to $60 billion by FY28.Importantly, consumer expectations are changing alongside the expansion of the market. Bain's research found that more than 70 percent of surveyed Indian consumers expected convenience and quality care to help them manage their health proactively. The use of digital health care applications, including telemedicine, e-pharmacy and wellness services, had increased by 20 to 100 percent during the pandemic. The report also pointed to the growing demand for integrated health care models that offer consumers a single point of access to multiple services.This is the space Nivara hopes to address by bringing different aspects of health care delivery under one umbrella.The entry comes at a time when India's organised hospital sector is expanding rapidly. Apollo Hospitals, one of the country's largest health care chains, reported a network of 78 hospitals and 10,970 beds in FY26, alongside more than 2,500 diagnostic centres. Max Healthcare, meanwhile, had an operational capacity of 5,518 beds at the end of September. Both companies have announced substantial capacity expansion plans.For Nivara, the proposition is that bringing services together can make health care easier to access and navigate, while also directing patients to the most appropriate and potentially less expensive setting for treatment.But building such a network will require more than capital. The company will need to attract medical talent, establish clinical credibility and ensure consistent standards across different formats of care. Its subscription model will also have to demonstrate that it can deliver value to patients while remaining commercially viable.For now, the Bajaj family is keeping its ambitions national, but its execution local. Pune will be the laboratory in which Nivara tests its integrated health care model before attempting to replicate it in other cities. The bigger test will be whether a business built around keeping patients out of hospitals as much as possible can emerge as a meaningful new player in India's increasingly competitive health care market.

The group believes that nearly 70 percent of health care problems can be addressed outside hospitals, and wants to build its network around this premise.
The first step will be a medical centre at Amanora in Pune, which is scheduled to open next week.
The facility will bring together diagnostics, medical testing, doctor consultations and physiotherapy under one roof.
Patients will be able to access their medical reports in one place, while the centre will also have a dedicated play area for children.
The Pune launch is significant for a family that has deep roots in the city.
Bajaj Auto and Bajaj Finance, two of the group's flagship businesses, are headquartered in Pune.
The health care venture will initially use the city as a testing ground before taking its model to other markets.
Nivara aims to establish a presence in six cities over 10 years.
The next layer of the network will comprise home health care services and day-surgery centres.
These centres will offer procedures and treatments such as dialysis, chemotherapy and endoscopy, among others, allowing patients to access services without having to visit a full-fledged hospital..
It is likely to take three to four years to complete.

The group had earlier announced an investment of ₹2,500 crore in its health care venture, which is being built as a continuum of care spanning neighbourhood medical centres, ambulatory facilities, home health care and multispecialty hospitals.
One of the more interesting aspects of Nivara's proposed model is a subscription-based offering.
Under this, customers would pay a monthly fee to cover their outpatient health care requirements.
The company is also considering extending the offering to cover surgeries." We plan to add an option that allows subscription patients to be covered for everything, including surgeries," Bajaj said.
The contours of this offering, including how it will be priced and whether the surgical component will involve an insurance arrangement, are yet to be spelt out.

The distinction will be important in a market where outpatient expenses account for a significant part of household health care spending but are not adequately covered by traditional health insurance policies.
The Bajaj group has an insurance business, but Bajaj clarified that it would operate independently of the health care venture.
Nivara would deal with all insurance providers on an equal footing, with the relationship being conducted at arm's length.
The opportunity is considerable.
The report also estimated the health care innovation opportunity at $30 billion in FY23, with the potential to double to $60 billion by FY28.

Bain's research found that more than 70 percent of surveyed Indian consumers expected convenience and quality care to help them manage their health proactively.
The report also pointed to the growing demand for integrated health care models that offer consumers a single point of access to multiple services.
This is the space Nivara hopes to address by bringing different aspects of health care delivery under one umbrella.
The entry comes at a time when India's organised hospital sector is expanding rapidly.
Apollo Hospitals, one of the country's largest health care chains, reported a network of 78 hospitals and 10,970 beds in FY26, alongside more than 2,500 diagnostic centres.
Max Healthcare, meanwhile, had an operational capacity of 5,518 beds at the end of September.
Both companies have announced substantial capacity expansion plans.

For Nivara, the proposition is that bringing services together can make health care easier to access and navigate, while also directing patients to the most appropriate and potentially less expensive setting for treatment.
But building such a network will require more than capital.
The company will need to attract medical talent, establish clinical credibility and ensure consistent standards across different formats of care.
Its subscription model will also have to demonstrate that it can deliver value to patients while remaining commercially viable.
For now, the Bajaj family is keeping its ambitions national, but its execution local.
Pune will be the laboratory in which Nivara tests its integrated health care model before attempting to replicate it in other cities.

The bigger test will be whether a business built around keeping patients out of hospitals as much as possible can emerge as a meaningful new player in India's increasingly competitive health care market.

stories.headline: Supreme Court upholds tribal land rights, quashes mining-linked acquisition in Odisha
stories.title: Supreme Court upholds tribal land rights, quashes mining-linked acquisition in Odisha
stories.summary: Court says prior Gram Sabha consent was mandatory under the 2013 land acquisition law; sets aside acquisition for Dalmia Cement’s mining project in Sundargarh
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court has stuck down the process of land acquisition for limestone mining in Odisha’s Sundargarh district after observing that the prior consent of the concerned Gram Sabha was mandatory for land acquisition in the Scheduled Areas, as per Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

Hearing the case of Bibol Toppo versus Odisha government and others, wherein acquisition of lands by the Odisha government for the purpose of mining by Dalmia Cements Bharat Limited was challenged, a Supreme Court bench comprising Justices Dipankar Datta and Justice Satish Chandra Sharma ruled that the land cannot be acquired without prior consent of the Gram Sabha as per Section 41 of the 2013 Act.
“In finality we allow the writ petition and hold that the land acquisition in question is unsustainable.
The acquisition, along with the relevant notifications and orders is hereby set aside,” Supreme Court judges ruled.

The appellants were residents of Kukuda, Bihabandha and Lanjiberna villages in Odisha’s Sundargarh district, challenging land acquisition initiated by the State government for Dalmia Cement Bharat Limited.
The State Government had granted a mining lease to the company for conducting mining operations over an area of 893.55 Ha.
The company held the mining lease, extended until February 2040, but sought to acquire 273.57 hectares of the land across the three villages to obtain surface rights required for mining operations.
The land acquisition was challenged in Orissa High Court.
The court had held that the requirement of prior consent did not apply as it was an acquisition by the State, as the State was being clothed with the right, title or interest in the land.

The court had further held that even if the requirement of obtaining prior consent of 80% land owners was applicable, the process of taking consent ought to be a continuing process which takes place through the various stages of the acquisition proceedings.
On the basis of this position, the court had acknowledged that a total 535 affected persons have given their consent in Form J as per Odisha Rules of 2013 Act, which satisfies the legal requirement.
Petitioner Mr. Toppo, however, submitted that the provisions of prior consent are mandatory and not directory.

stories.headline: Karnataka Cabinet clears projects worth ₹4,000 crore for Bengaluru city, approves ₹10,250 crore for development of nine State Highways
stories.title: Karnataka Cabinet clears projects worth ₹4,000 crore for Bengaluru city, approves ₹10,250 crore for development of nine State Highways
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'cabinet clears' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Karnataka government on Thursday approved projects worth over ₹4,000 crore for Bengaluru city, while also approving development of nine State Highways at a cost of around ₹10,250 crore.
The Cabinet approved distribution of 5 lakh sites as part of Bhoo Guarantee by December or January for which 24,000 acres of government land has been identified.

The Cabinet approved suspension and investigation to be instituted by the Governor against Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC) member B.V. Geetha, who has been arrested by the Special Investigation Team in connection with the recruitment scam.

About 730-km stretch of road on nine State Highways in Mysuru, Mandya, Chamarajanagar, Kodagu, Hassan, Bengaluru South, Vijayapura, Kalaburagi, Belagavi, Bagalkot, Koppal, and Gadag district will be developed at a cost of around ₹10,252 crore.
Approval was given to deploy 2,000 electric buses on gross cost contract scheme at a cost of ₹1,700 crore, including World Bank assistance of ₹1,400 crore.

While 1,000 buses would be provided to Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation, 500 buses each will be provided to Kittur Rani Chennamma Road Transport Corporation and Kalyana Karnataka Road Transport Corporation.
Among the projects approved for Bengaluru are the white-topping of 130 km stretch of 88 roads in the city at a cost ₹2,321 crore by Bengaluru Smart Infrastructure Ltd.
and elevating the outer ring road stretch between Silk Board Junction and K.R. Puram Metro Station to global standards at a revised cost of ₹486 crore.

Other Cabinet decisions on Thursday included approval of purchase and distribution of laptops at a cost of ₹50,000 each to 5,000 students belonging to minority communities studying in B.E. and BCA courses.

The Cabinet did not agree to the proposal by Minority Welfare, Haj and Wakf Department for direct cash transfers to students, and instead directed the department to purchase the laptops for distribution.

It also agreed waive interest amount of ₹236.06 crore on repayment of principal by beneficiaries for loans sanctioned by seven development corporations under Backward Classes Welfare Department between 2013 and 2021 under a one-time payment scheme.
Beneficiaries have in total defaulted payment of ₹577 crore, Deputy Chief Minister G. Parameshwara said in the post Cabinet briefing.

stories.headline: Supreme Court directs verification, remedial measures against bogus Form-7s in Delhi’s Mustafabad
stories.title: Supreme Court directs verification, remedial measures against bogus Form-7s in Delhi’s Mustafabad
stories.summary: The petition drew attention to an investigation by The Hindu, which reported that 28 electors against whom deletion applications had been submitted were physically traced at the addresses at which they were enrolled
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Thursday (November 19, 2026) directed authorities to verify allegations that fabricated Form-7s were filed to delete genuine voters from electoral rolls in Delhi’s Mustafabad Assembly Constituency during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process and take all remedial measures.

A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant even urged Congress leader Ali Mehdi, represented by advocate Shariq Ahmed, to approach the jurisdictional magistrate if the police have refused to register an FIR on his complaint about fabrication and forgery.
The order was passed on Mr. Mehdi’s plea that a “substantial” number of ghost Form-7s seeking deletion of voters had been detected, and that a crisis of electoral integrity is brewing.

The writ petition said that voters whose names were put forward for deletion on the grounds of death, absence, or permanent shifting were found to be very much alive, present, and residing at their recorded addresses on the electoral roll.
The persons in whose names Form-7s had been filed for deletion of these voters deny having filed or signed on the applications.
“The integrity of an electoral roll is compromised not only when an ineligible name remains upon it.
It is equally compromised when an eligible elector is removed from it on a fact which never existed or upon an objection which the supposed objector never made.
The present record discloses the latter danger in its stark form,” the writ petition said.
It said persons declared dead were alive, while persons said to have shifted were found at home.
Of the 37 applications examined by electoral authorities, 36 were found to be false or fabricated.
“The existence of a genuine objector and the existence of a genuine ground for deletion — In Mustafabad, both are under serious doubt at the same time,” Mr. Ahmed submitted.

Section 22 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 requires the Electoral Registration Officer to be satisfied, after proper verification of the facts, before an entry can be corrected or deleted.

stories.headline: Delhi court asks for action taken report on sexual harassment complaint against ACP despite police’s closure claim in Supreme Court
stories.title: Delhi court asks for action taken report on sexual harassment complaint against ACP despite police’s closure claim in Supreme Court
stories.summary: The Court directed that the response be filed “point-wise”, addressing each of its queries and detailing the action taken on the complaint before the complainant approached the Court
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: A Delhi court has sought a detailed account of the police action on the complaint filed by a journalist who accused Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) Vivek Bhagat of groping her while she was covering the detention of student leader Neha Bora at Jantar Mantar on October 3.
On November 16, the Delhi.

Police told the Supreme Court that sexual assault cases by three women journalists during the anti-SIR protests in the Capital in October were ‘closed’, while in a fourth case, no video evidence was found to warrant further proceedings.

In an order dated November 3, accessed by The Hindu, Judicial Magistrate First Class Kautuk Bhardwaj of the Patiala House Courts directed the Station House Officer (SHO) concerned to submit an action taken report (ATR), answering five specific questions about the complaint and the subsequent police inquiry.
The Court asked the SHO to state whether the complaint had been received at the police station and, if so, what action had been taken.
It also sought details on whether the investigation or inquiry established the commission of any cognisable offence against the accused and whether any action followed.
If an FIR had been registered, the police were asked to provide its status and the progress of the investigation.
If no cognisable offence had been made out, the SHO was required to clarify whether the complainant had been informed of the decision.
The Court directed that the response be filed “point-wise”, addressing each of its queries and detailing the action taken on the complaint before the complainant approached the Court.
The Court also directed the SHO to take all necessary steps within three days of receiving the order to preserve the relevant CCTV footage and other digital evidence, including body-camera footage.
The compliance report on the preservation of the evidence is to be filed within a week.
The matter is listed for December 1 for the filing of the ATR.
